questions.question: Which language should the marketing workspace use?
questions.rationale: TypeScript is a practical default for a multi-business marketing workspace.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Recommended for a typed, maintainable web application.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Choose this for a JavaScript-only frontend.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should the workspace use?
questions.rationale: React is the default choice for a new TypeScript web workspace.

options.label: React
options.description: A flexible component-based framework with a broad ecosystem.

questions.question: What should a business owner be able to do in the workspace? For example, manage a business profile, review campaign drafts, and track leads.
questions.answer: Manage a business profile, review and edit campaign drafts, and track customer inquiries.
questions.rationale: These are a useful starting set of workflows for a customer-acquisition assistant.
questions.recommendedChoice: Manage a business profile, review and edit campaign drafts, and track customer inquiries.

questions.question: Which language should the marketing assistant API use?
questions.rationale: TypeScript keeps the initial application stack consistent.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Recommended for sharing types and skills across the frontend and API.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Choose this for a JavaScript-only backend.

options.label: Python
options.description: Choose this if the team prefers Python for API and AI integration work.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Choose this if the team prefers the .NET ecosystem.

questions.question: Which framework should power the marketing assistant API?
questions.rationale: Azure Functions is the standard Azure API framework recommendation when no custom framework has been specified.

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: A managed serverless option for API and event-driven workloads.

questions.question: Is the first example business an aesthetician or beauty salon? What customer-acquisition outcome should it focus on, and which channels matter most (for example, appointment inquiries from Instagram, Google, email, or a website)? Mention any integrations you want, or say to start with campaign drafts only.
questions.answer: Start with an aesthetician or beauty salon; create human-reviewed campaign drafts focused on more appointment inquiries, initially for Instagram and Google, without automatic publishing.
questions.rationale: The first business type and preferred acquisition channels are not yet clear; the default keeps publishing under the owner's control.
questions.recommendedChoice: Start with an aesthetician or beauty salon; create human-reviewed campaign drafts focused on more appointment inquiries, initially for Instagram and Google, without automatic publishing.

questions.question: Which data stores should the project use?
questions.rationale: Business profiles and campaign history need persistence; Azure Functions also requires an associated storage account.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Store business profiles, campaigns, leads, and user-managed settings.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Store files and provide the storage account associated with Azure Functions.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Choose only if the application does not need persistent data or Azure Functions storage.

questions.question: Should business owners sign in to manage their own business profiles and campaigns?
questions.rationale: The product is intended for multiple businesses, so each client should have a private workspace.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Each business owner signs in to access and manage their workspace.

options.label: No
options.description: The initial application has no sign-in for business owners.
